questions.stem: In a class of 30 students, 18 study French, 12 study Spanish and 5 study both. How many students study neither language?
questions.explanation: Using the addition formula: French or Spanish = 18 + 12 − 5 = 25. Neither = 30 − 25 = 5. A common error is forgetting to subtract the overlap, giving 30 − 30 = 0.

questions.stem: From the Venn diagram: A only = 8, B only = 12, A and B = 6, neither = 4. A student is chosen at random. Find P(A).
questions.explanation: Total = 8 + 12 + 6 + 4 = 30. A includes A only + A and B = 8 + 6 = 14. P(A) = 14/30 = 7/15. A common error is using only the 'A only' region (8/30).

questions.stem: In a survey of 50 people: 30 like coffee, 25 like tea, 10 like neither. How many like both coffee and tea?
questions.explanation: Like at least one = 50 − 10 = 40. Using the addition rule: Coffee + Tea − Both = at least one. 30 + 25 − Both = 40. Both = 55 − 40 = 15.

questions.stem: From a Venn diagram with sets A and B: P(A) = 0.6, P(B) = 0.5, P(A and B) = 0.2. What is P(A or B)?
questions.explanation: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B) = 0.6 + 0.5 − 0.2 = 0.9. Option (a) forgets to subtract the intersection. You must subtract P(A and B) to avoid double-counting.

questions.stem: In a group of 40 students: 22 play football, 17 play rugby, 8 play both. A student who plays football is chosen at random. What is the probability this student also plays rugby?
questions.explanation: Given the student plays football, we restrict to the 22 football players. Of these, 8 also play rugby. P(rugby | football) = 8/22 = 4/11. Option (b) divides by rugby players instead. Option (a) uses the full group.
